A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, references, and complete appendices. Renumbered sections and proofs can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 6.3 and Figure 2 report an original numerical comparison of proxy and faithful conditioning in a synthetic 100-arm Beta-reward bandit, including improvement across success thresholds.

after.justification: Section 7.3 and Figure 2 retain the original synthetic-bandit numerical results. The newly added policy-gradient discussion and estimator are theoretical, without additional empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The success-conditioned policy and imitation objective remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 formalize iterated fitting and REINFORCE for comparison; they do not establish a modification to the existing success-conditioning method.

E1.justification: The same two-arm example and 100-arm Beta-reward bandit are retained. No additional dataset, application domain, or evaluated task is introduced.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains proxy versus faithful conditioning. REINFORCE is newly analyzed theoretically, but is not added to a reported empirical comparison.

E3.justification: The bandit retains 99 symmetric Beta arms with parameters drawn from Uniform(0.3, 0.7), one Beta(18, 2) arm, and a uniform behavior policy. No evaluated settings change; Appendix A describes an estimator without reporting its experimental use.

E4.justification: The return-threshold sensitivity illustration and its findings are unchanged. The new policy-gradient derivation and diagnostic estimator are not additional ablation, robustness, or empirical error analyses.

E5.justification: New Appendix A specifies an estimator averaging independent held-out successful trajectories, states unbiasedness and consistency, and explains the bias from substituting realized actions for full action distributions. No repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Both figures retain identical plotted content. Example 3.1 still improves success from 0.5 to 0.50005, and Figure 2 retains the same threshold-dependent gains and eventual negative improvement. No empirical result entries are added.

T1.justification: New Lemma 5.1 derives the equivalence between the success-imitation gradient at the behavior policy and the REINFORCE gradient, up to scaling. Appendix A adds the diagnostic estimator and its statistical justification. The principal theorems and existing appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contribution statements retain the trust-region equivalence, action-influence identity, conservative improvement claim, and return-thresholding tradeoff. The additions do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds an interpretation of single-step on-policy updates versus multiple supervised steps using a frozen behavior policy, explaining data reuse and suggesting exploratory data collection. Section 2.1 also clarifies the distinction between conditioning trajectories on success and executing the conditioned policy.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 document behavior-policy freezing, inner updates, and refresh timing. Appendix A supplies a concrete diagnostic computation using held-out successful trajectories and full next-action distributions, requiring one forward pass per model at each visited state.

R1.justification: New Section 5 explicitly positions REINFORCE as an incremental, on-policy special case of success conditioning. The bibliography and the existing comparisons with trust-region methods, return conditioning, and control as inference are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The revision inserts Section 5 and Appendix A, updates subsequent numbering, adds acknowledgments and an impact statement, and makes localized explanatory and editorial corrections. Most existing prose and the overall argument retain their original structure.

P2.justification: The paper receives a document-wide ICML-style reformat, including a redesigned title and affiliation block, running headers, changed spacing, and removal of shaded theorem boxes. Both figures are relocated within the columns, and two algorithm displays are added; the plotted content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 5 clarifies the relationship to policy gradients, while Appendix A turns v1's diagnostic-computability statement into an explicit estimation recipe with a useful bias qualification. These improve understanding and practical usability, while the central theory and numerical evidence remain unchanged.
